tasks.short: Manage delivery against the approved project budget, schedule and scope.

steps.what: Read the project plan, delivery updates and financial actuals.
Combine costs, dates and scope changes in a control workbook.
Assess variances and prepare feasible recovery options.
Negotiate recovery commitments and trade-offs with delivery and business leads.
Approve or reject changes beyond the project manager's delegated limits.
Update the baseline, actions and change register after the decision.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration joins approved baselines in the {PROJECT} with actuals and commitments from the {ERP}, feeding a variance dashboard in the {BI}. Configured approvals in the {WORKFLOW} record change decisions and update the {PROJECT}; people assess recovery options and negotiate commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Financial periods, project identifiers and baselines differ across systems. Recovery choices also depend on commitments that are rarely recorded consistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and configured approvals cover much of the flow. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the remaining mappings and checks, but the speedup needs measurement.
tasks.still_hard: Reliable cost allocation, incomplete commitments and contested scope remain expensive. A dashboard cannot settle competing business priorities.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparent progress hides delivery risk, negotiate credible commitments and accept responsibility for trade-offs.

ambition.what: Weekly recovery decisions for projects breaching agreed cost or schedule tolerances

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling control reports to testing recovery choices with delivery leads. The project manager can gain authority to adjust sequencing within explicit sponsor-approved tolerances; budget increases still need approval.

reach.task: Assess whether recovery options preserve the project's business benefits.
reach.learn: Benefit modelling, sensitivity analysis and the difference between sunk costs and future commitments.

evidence.claim: Deterministic joins, tolerance checks and configured approvals can support project control; this design is an implementation estimate.
GitHub Copilot offers coding and review assistance, with oversight expected; this supports build feasibility, not a specific speedup.
METR found experienced developers slower in its early-2025 study; its later rerun was inconclusive. Coding acceleration should be validated locally.

assumptions: The baseline scenario uses the {PROJECT} for delivery, the {ERP} for costs and a workbook to reconcile them.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates of active task effort, excluding waiting.
Build ranges cover a pilot with one project portfolio and one finance integration; ranges may overlap.
The design uses project-level measures and excludes individual staff scoring. GDPR and EU AI Act applicability require assessment; consultation follows national rules.
unknowns: Whether project identifiers connect actuals, purchase commitments and delivery records.
Which tolerances and baseline changes the project manager may approve.
Whether configured integration and approval features are already licensed.
Required access approvals and whether employee consultation is needed.
research_questions: Which existing configuration can replace custom integration?
How accurately do recorded actuals and commitments predict the next reporting period?
Which variance alerts lead to a useful management decision?
new_work: Resolve unmatched financial records and stale baselines.
Maintain cost mappings, reporting periods and tolerance rules.
Review integration failures and audit approved baseline updates.

tasks.short: Work with project personnel to understand problems and agree practical resolutions.

steps.what: Read issue records, delivery updates and relevant team messages.
Prepare an issue brief with evidence, open questions and affected dependencies.

loop.input: Authorised issue records and explicitly linked messages, plus the project baseline.
loop.output: An issue brief separating reported facts, disagreements and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require source references for factual statements; the project manager checks omissions and sensitive wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per issue; missing or conflicting evidence returns to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template can organise the brief, but relevant explanations and disagreements appear in free text.

steps.what: Discuss causes, constraints and disagreements with the people involved.
Agree a technical resolution and identify changes requiring escalation.
Record the agreed resolution, action owners and due dates.
Send follow-ups when agreed actions become overdue.

tasks.design: The {PROJECT} supplies issue records and explicitly linked {CHAT} messages to a bounded drafting loop that prepares a source-linked brief in the {DOCS}. People discuss the problem and approve the resolution, while structured decisions feed configured action records and reminders in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The useful context sits across messages and issue records. The central conversation involves trust, disagreement and incomplete technical knowledge.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded model can prepare a brief from a limited evidence set. Existing action forms and reminders can handle the paperwork once people agree.
tasks.still_hard: People may conceal uncertainty, disagree about causes or lack capacity to deliver the proposed fix. Better preparation does not remove those constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Create enough trust for people to admit problems, challenge an attractive explanation and negotiate a workable commitment.

ambition.what: A recurring cross-team dependency resolution clinic

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into reconstructing issues and chasing routine actions. The project manager can convene cross-team resolution sessions; technical decisions and scope approvals retain their existing owners.

reach.task: Trace a recurring project blocker to an interface or requirements mismatch.
reach.learn: Dependency mapping, requirements validation and evidence-based root-cause analysis.

evidence.claim: Configured action registers and reminders can automate follow-up while the resolution conversation remains human.
TOPdesk summarises tickets and drafts knowledge items for review, demonstrating related bounded text preparation.

assumptions: Only issue-linked, authorised messages enter the brief; private conversations are excluded.
Agreed decisions are captured in structured fields during the discussion.
The technical lead may approve technical resolutions within existing scope; change requests follow sponsor approval.
Time shares and build ranges are pilot estimates. GDPR access controls and national consultation requirements apply.
unknowns: Whether issue records contain links to the relevant evidence.
Which discussions may be processed and under what retention policy.
Who can approve technical resolutions and cross-team commitments.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed message processing.
research_questions: Does a source-linked brief reduce preparation time without suppressing disagreement?
Which issue types benefit from a brief, and which are quicker to discuss directly?
Can existing action forms capture commitments without creating duplicate records?
new_work: Check brief sources, omissions and disputed statements.
Maintain message access boundaries and brief templates.
Handle disputed reminders and actions lacking an accepted owner.

tasks.short: Track milestones and deliverables, verify progress and surface exceptions.

steps.what: Inspect milestone dates, task completion and dependencies in the project record.
Ask delivery owners for missing dates, evidence and dependency updates.
Provide a progress update and links to deliverable evidence.
Reconcile owner updates and baseline dates in the tracking workbook.
Review weak evidence, conflicting updates and likely milestone slippage with delivery owners.
Publish milestone status and exception notes for project control.

tasks.design: Configure the {PROJECT} with milestone baselines, evidence links, owner update forms and stale-record reminders, removing the reconciliation workbook. A dashboard in the {PROJECT} shows date variance, blocked dependencies and evidence gaps, then publishes a standard status view after exceptions are resolved.
tasks.previous_blocker: Updates arrive as messages while baseline dates live elsewhere. Completion labels are often mistaken for evidence of an accepted deliverable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project fields, forms and dashboards can handle most tracking. Small deterministic extensions can check dependency dates and missing evidence without a model.
tasks.still_hard: An apparently complete task may conceal unfinished integration or acceptance work. Credible forecasts still depend on delivery owners reporting uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge optimistic progress claims and distinguish administrative completion from usable delivery.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly dependency resequencing for threatened milestones

tasks.altitude: The week centres on evidence gaps and blocked dependencies instead of collecting routine updates. The project manager can gain authority to resequence work within the approved baseline, with milestone changes still following change control.

reach.task: Analyse dependency paths and forecast milestone confidence.
reach.learn: Critical-path analysis, forecast calibration and acceptance evidence design.

evidence.claim: Structured milestone fields, baseline comparisons, reminders and dashboards can handle routine tracking without a model.
Removing workbook reconciliation requires owners to update the authoritative project record rather than a separate message chain.

assumptions: The baseline scenario includes a workbook bridging project records and owner messages; companies with integrated tracking may already avoid this work.
The future dashboard replaces the milestone comparison artefact, so no separate workbook is maintained.
Structured owner updates remain human; the design does not infer completion from message activity.
Shares, remaining time and build ranges are estimates. Access and any consultation follow GDPR and national rules.
unknowns: Whether the {PROJECT} supports baselines, dependency checks and owner forms.
Which evidence is required before a deliverable counts as complete.
How often owners update records and how stale updates are handled.
Whether the proposed visibility changes trigger employee consultation.
research_questions: Which existing tracking fields can replace the workbook?
Do evidence-gap alerts identify slippage earlier than completion percentages?
What reminder frequency improves updates without creating noise?
new_work: Maintain milestone definitions, evidence requirements and dependency links.
Resolve stale updates and inconsistent completion claims.
Review alert usefulness and repair broken evidence links.

tasks.short: Check deliverable quality, secure release approval and submit the approved package.

steps.what: Collect the deliverable version, acceptance criteria and quality evidence.
Check required tests, documents, approvals and version consistency.
Compare narrative evidence with acceptance criteria and identify unexplained gaps.

loop.input: Version-pinned acceptance criteria and linked narrative quality evidence.
loop.output: A criterion-by-criterion evidence map with supported, missing and uncertain findings.
loop.check: Require criterion identifiers and evidence references; the quality lead verifies every proposed finding.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction pass per package; missing sources or ambiguity leave the criterion unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules check required files and test outcomes, but narrative evidence uses different wording from acceptance criteria.

steps.what: Judge fitness for use and recommend release, rework or an explicit waiver.
Approve submission of the specified version and any permitted quality waiver.
Submit the approved version to the agreed recipient.
Record submission evidence and link the receipt to the deliverable.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} assembles a version-pinned package from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT}, runs deterministic completeness checks and requests a bounded evidence-map draft for narrative criteria. The quality lead reviews fitness for use, the business owner approves submission, and the project manager confirms the recipient before the {EMAIL} sends the package and the {PROJECT} records delivery evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Deliverables, test evidence and approvals refer to different versions. Narrative acceptance criteria resist simple completeness checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Version identifiers and configured approvals can bind checks to the exact package. A bounded model can draft an evidence map for review without deciding acceptance.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence can be incomplete or misleading, and passing tests does not prove fitness for use. Contractual acceptance and quality waivers require authorised judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether the deliverable meets the real business need and recognise defects that a checklist misses.

ambition.what: Pre-submission readiness reviews for small internal IT projects

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling packages and chasing approval evidence to resolving material quality gaps. The project manager gains clearer authority to block submission when required evidence is missing; acceptance and waiver rights remain with authorised owners.

reach.task: Design acceptance controls and analyse recurring deliverable defects.
reach.learn: Evidence traceability, risk-based sampling and corrective-action verification.

evidence.claim: Version-bound completeness checks and approval workflows can automate package handling while preserving human release authority.
SharePoint autofill columns demonstrates prompt-based document metadata extraction and warns of errors; it does not establish acceptance-review reliability.

assumptions: The scenario includes submission to an external recipient; internal-only projects can use an internal delivery action.
Mandatory quality controls cannot be waived unless policy and contract explicitly permit it.
A changed package invalidates earlier checks and approval; failed checks return rework actions to the delivery owner.
A submission receipt proves delivery, not business acceptance.
Build ranges cover package handling and evidence mapping, excluding development of new technical test suites.
Time estimates require pilot validation. GDPR, EU AI Act applicability and consultation under national rules must be assessed.
unknowns: Which quality checks are mandatory and which evidence is machine-readable.
Who may approve submission, accept deliverables and authorise waivers.
Whether recipients use the {EMAIL}, the {PARTNER_PORTAL} or another approved channel.
Whether contracts require signatures or a separate acceptance process.
Access, retention and consultation requirements for the evidence set.
research_questions: Which quality checks can run deterministically against versioned evidence?
How often does the draft evidence map miss material gaps or cite irrelevant evidence?
Can existing approval configuration invalidate approval automatically when the package changes?
new_work: Review evidence maps and correct unsupported coverage findings.
Maintain quality checklists, acceptance mappings and waiver permissions.
Handle failed submissions, recipient changes and missing receipts.
Investigate version mismatches and verify approval invalidation.

role.altitude: The project manager spends less time collecting status, reconciling records and assembling submissions. More of the week goes to delivery trade-offs, difficult conversations and evidence-based readiness decisions, with delegated sequencing and escalation rights made explicit.
reach: Management analyst: compare recovery choices against business benefits.
Computer systems analyst: investigate recurring requirements and interface blockers.
Project management specialist: improve dependency forecasts and milestone evidence.
Quality control systems manager: strengthen acceptance controls and corrective actions.
skills_to_grow: Data reconciliation and project control design
Bounded model evaluation and source verification
GDPR-aware access design and consultation under national rules
role.ambitious_version: Run a lightweight delivery assurance service that combines frequent recovery decisions, cross-team blocker clinics and pre-submission readiness reviews for projects too small to receive dedicated assurance support.
